newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called up after ACCESS, cash holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called up after ACCESS, cash holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Wednesday after a stronger ACCESS session and early talk of steady cash prices, market sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.22 to $2.23 at 0935 EDT after settling Tuesday at $2.189 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, June last traded 2.6 cents firmer at $2.215, near the session high.
Meanwhile, cash prices at Henry Hub, La., were talked at $2.18-2.21 amid warmer temperatures in Texas.

A high of 87 degrees F is forecast for Houston today, Weather Services Corp said, while cooler-than-normal weather is expected to continue throughout the Northeast and Midwest over the next few days. Sweltering temperatures are blanketing parts of the Southwest, with Phoenix expected to experience a high of 101 degrees F today and 102 degrees Thursday.

Technically, traders pegged June support at $2.14-2.15, and then around $2.05. Heavy selling was expected to surface once June hits $2.25, one trader said. Further resistance was seen at $2.28-29 and the contract high of $2.43.
Estimates for a build in today's weekly AGA storage report ranged from 50 to 80 bcf, versus a gain of 63 bcf a year ago.

In Tuesday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices slipped more than five cents to $2.15-2.19. Midcon pipes were down a similar amount to the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas skidded several cents to the low-$2.40s.
Maintenance work on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through next Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
